reasons: No tests are included for this file.
The pop-up styling relies on many specific selectors in the cmdk library.

terms.meaning: a library that provides a searchable list with keyboard navigation
a pop-up window that sits above the page
a labeled set of related entries inside a list

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Command box frame
sections.what: Sets up the main command box that holds the search and the list, with rounded corners and a popover-style background. Content that overflows is clipped.
sections.why: Gives the list a consistent frame across the app.
sections.watch_out: Clipping means long lists must scroll inside the frame rather than grow beyond it.

sections.name: CommandDialog (part 1)
sections.title: Pop-up, search box, list and empty message
sections.what: Wraps the command box in a pop-up window. It draws a search box with a search icon, a scrollable list with a maximum height, and the message shown when nothing matches.
sections.why: Lets the command list open on demand, like a quick-find menu.
sections.watch_out: The list height is capped at a fixed pixel size, so long content scrolls rather than growing the box.

sections.name: CommandDialog (part 2)
sections.title: Groups, dividers, items and shortcut hints
sections.what: Styles the groups of related entries with small headings, the thin dividing lines, each selectable entry, and the faded keyboard shortcut text on the right.
sections.why: Groups and highlights help users scan the list and use the keyboard.
sections.watch_out: Highlighting depends on a selected-state marker set by the cmdk library, and without it no entry looks highlighted.

sections.name: CommandDialog (part 3)
sections.title: Exported parts
sections.what: Makes the command parts available to other files. Nothing is shown on its own.
sections.why: Pages import these names to build a command box.
sections.watch_out: A new part must be added to this list before any page can use it.

summary: A searchable list of commands or choices, with an optional pop-up version.
purpose: Lets users type to find an item in a list, such as a quick-find menu.
why: Likely reason: a styled wrapper around the cmdk library, with a dialog option for pop-up use. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Step 1: Loads the cmdk library, the dialog and the search icon. Step 2: Builds the outer command box. Step 3: Builds the pop-up version, the search box, the scrollable list and the empty message. Step 4: Builds groups, dividers, selectable items and shortcut hints. Step 5: Makes all parts available to other files.
inputs: Groups and items placed inside, the search text the user types, and optional settings for the pop-up dialog.
outputs: A search box with a filtered list on screen. The pop-up version appears in a dialog.
risks: The pop-up version depends on the dialog file, so a change there affects it. The styling of the pop-up contains many very specific selectors, so small changes to the list layout can break it.
debug: If the list is empty, check that items sit inside the list part and that the search text matches them. If the pop-up does not open, check that the dialog's open control is connected. If the search finds nothing, check the empty message and the search text.
